messages:
elaine: Quick follow-up from the quant profiles RFC — proposal to expose a per-endpoint 'quality_budget' (0-100) that the runtime uses to pick precision lanes (FP8/INT8/4bit) and fallback thresholds. Wanted to sync on API shape + migration plan.

mike: Strong +1 on having a single numeric budget. Simpler for product. How does this map to our existing precision profiles?

elaine: idea: profiles remain as runtime artifacts (profiles/weights-calibration), budget is just a hint. Mapping table in config: e.g. 85-100 => FP8-primary, 60-84 => INT8, 0-59 => 4bit+aggressive-fallback. Runtime still consults per-model calibration scores and per-customer overrides.

noah: Where does per-request override live? Header or body? We should avoid open-ended overrides for hosted.

elaine: default: allow per-request 'x-redwood-quality-budget' header for dedicated/private. Hosted: only allow via pinned route config or opt-in flag. This avoids abuse and SLO surprises.

jamal: +1. Need a sample API snippet for SDKs and gateway. Also how does this interact with streaming and token-by-token fallback?

elaine: draft API header: 
```
x-redwood-quality-budget: 78
```
Runtime behavior: budget is evaluated at request start. If model enters degradation mid-stream (deg-score jump), runtime will attempt fallbacks: first switch quant lane, then route to compatible higher-precision variant, finally apply cached partial prefix from KP cache.

noah: We must define a clear degradation score threshold that triggers fallback; otherwise variant hopping could cause instability. Suggest deg-score > 0.15 for sustained 3 tokens.

jamal: Also need telemetry flags: attach 'quality_budget' and 'applied_lane' to traces + reason code when fallback used. That helps SRE/product rollback.

calib-bot: FYI — offline calibration lib can produce per-model "quality_curve" CSV: budget -> expected perplexity delta. Upload endpoint: POST /models/:id/calibration.

elaine: Good — we'll require an uploaded quality_curve for any model we allow to be used with aggressive budgets (<50). Validation rules: curve must include >=5 points, monotonicity enforced, and an estimated 95% CI.

mike: Migration: existing customers without budgets default to 100 (conservative). New route config flag 'allow_budget' must be enabled to accept header. Rollout plan: opt-in beta for 2 weeks then gradual opt-out.

noah: For Dedicated/Private, ops will want a global policy to cap min budget per customer to prevent large regressions. Add 'min_budget' at account level.

elaine: Yep. Account-level 'min_budget' + route-level 'max_aggressive_windows' to limit frequency of lane switches. Also propose circuit breaker: more than 3 fallbacks in 60s => throttle aggressive lanes for 5m.

jamal: Tests: unit tests for budget->lane mapping, sim harness with perf+quality metrics, and an integration smoke that runs eval prompts (from our eval bank) across budgets and asserts quality deltas within the uploaded curve CI.

noah: Ops question: how much extra telemetry volume? Attaching applied_lane + reason + budget per request is small. But we need sampled token-level degscore traces only when fallback triggered.

elaine: Agreed. Sampled token traces at 1% baseline, 100% when fallback happens. We'll surface an Ops dashboard with rate of fallbacks by route and by model.

mike: Who owns the rollout? Eng-runtime for runtime changes, Eng-ML for calibration tooling and eval harness, DevEx for SDK/header docs, SRE for dashboards & alerts.

elaine: I'll assemble a short RFC follow-up doc with API examples and rollout checklist. Target: internal preview in 2 weeks. Action items: @mike write mapping table prototype, @noah propose deg-score thresholds and hysteresis, @jamal spec telemetry envelope, @calib-bot add calibration upload endpoint stub.

mike: I'll push a mapping table gist by EOD.

noah: I'll validate deg thresholds against recent eval runs and post results here.

jamal: I'll sketch dashboard mockups and alert rules.

calib-bot: calibration endpoint stub created: POST /v1/models/:id/calibration; accepts CSV or JSON-lines. Warnings emitted for non-monotonic curves.

elaine: Perfect. Thanks all — will follow up with the doc and link here when ready. :rocket:
